headline: 8 workers killed: Probe body to be formed over Sitakunda shipyard gas poisoning
summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury announced an investigation after toxic gas exposure claimed eight lives at a shipbreaking yard in Chattogram.
details: At least eight workers have died following suspected toxic gas exposure at a shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda, Chattogram. The incident has sparked urgent calls for accountability and safety reviews in the region's shipbreaking industry.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury visited an injured worker at Chattogram Medical College Hospital on Friday, where he announced that a probe committee would be formed to investigate the cause of the tragedy.

The minister stated that further action would be taken based on the findings of the investigation. He noted that the situation was difficult to manage and that the army has been deployed to bring the area under control.
Reports indicate that the shipyard had previously faced legal action last month due to safety violations, raising concerns about systemic negligence in worker protection.
The incident occurred during ship-cutting operations, with some reports suggesting a lack of adequate safety measures were in place at the time of the gas leak.

headline: 153-run lead: Bangladesh take control of Darwin Test against Australia
summary: Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century and a dominant Day 2 performance leave Australia under immense pressure.
details: Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the Darwin Test in a commanding position, reaching 351 for 6 with a lead of 153 runs. This marks their second-best total in 13 Test innings against Australia.

Tanzid Hasan, playing only his second Test, scored his first Test century. The 25-year-old opener batted patiently for over five hours, striking eight fours and a six before being dismissed by Mitchell Starc.

The lead was built on strong partnerships, including a 102-run stand between Tanzid and Mominul Haque, a 93-run partnership with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, and a 66-run stand between Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim.

Australia's bowling attack found some rhythm with the second new ball, claiming three wickets in 4.5 overs. Steven Smith took all three catches at second slip, equaling Joe Root for the most catches by a non-wicketkeeper in Test history.
At stumps, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten. They added an unbroken 43-run partnership for the seventh wicket on an increasingly easy-paced Marrara pitch.

Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting described the Australian dressing room as a "nervous" place, stating that the home side is now "right behind the eight ball" and facing a critical test of their batting order.
